import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_1.csv"
]

# Columns expected in the target and source tables (schemas are identical)
target_columns = [
    'tripduration', 'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station id', 'start station name',
    'start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station id', 'end station name',
    'end station latitude', 'end station longitude', 'bikeid', 'usertype', 'birth year', 'gender'
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and in the same order
    df = df[target_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we can concatenate (union) them vertically
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Enforce data types as per target schema
# Define dtype mapping
dtype_map = {
    'tripduration': 'int64',
    'starttime': 'string',
    'stoptime': 'string',
    'start station id': 'Int64',  # Use pandas nullable integer dtype
    'start station name': 'string',
    'start station latitude': 'float64',
    'start station longitude': 'float64',
    'end station id': 'Int64',
    'end station name': 'string',
    'end station latitude': 'float64',
    'end station longitude': 'float64',
    'bikeid': 'Int64',
    'usertype': 'string',
    'birth year': 'Int64',
    'gender': 'Int64'
}

# Convert columns to target dtypes
for col, dtype in dtype_map.items():
    if dtype == 'string':
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('string')
    elif dtype == 'Int64':
        # Nullable integer type to handle possible missing values
        combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
    else:
        combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').astype(dtype)

# Save the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
